blocks.text: Mastering the Slack interface on your Mac

As a recruiter, you likely have dozens of channels open for different roles, hiring managers, and internal team updates. Staying on top of this requires more than just scrolling. Start by mastering the keyboard. Press Command + K to open the quick switcher. Type the name of the role you are currently hiring for to jump directly to that channel. This saves time compared to clicking through the sidebar.

If you are struggling to find a specific candidate mention, use the search modifiers. Type in:channelname to narrow your search to a specific project. You can also use from:username to find messages from a specific hiring manager. These small habits turn Slack from a noisy chat app into a structured database of candidate notes.

Recruiters lose significant time to manual data entry and context switching. You might spend hours moving information from an ATS like Workable into a Slack channel for hiring managers. Instead of copy and paste, use dictation. Hold the fn key to dictate your notes directly into the Slack message box. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your focus on the candidate profile.

items: Use Shift + Enter to create line breaks in your messages without sending them prematurely.
Pin important candidate requirements to the top of the channel using the three dots menu on any message.
Use /remind to set a follow up task for yourself regarding a candidate profile.
Clear your app cache via Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart if Slack feels slow during peak hiring hours.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to manage your Slack day

Lazur helps you manage your Mac without needing to hunt for buttons. If you are in a busy channel and need to find a specific document, hold Option + Command and ask Lazur where the file is. Lazur will point at the screen or answer out loud. You can also ask Lazur to guide you through complex settings, such as adjusting your notification schedule for specific channels.
Common mistakes recruiters make in Slack

One common mistake is keeping all notifications on for every channel. This creates constant interruptions that break your flow. Go to Slack Preferences by pressing Command + comma. Navigate to the Notifications tab and set your preferences to only notify you for mentions and direct messages. This keeps your focus on the work that actually requires your immediate attention.

Another mistake is not using threads. When you reply to a message in the main channel, it clutters the feed for everyone else. Always hover over the message and click the speech bubble icon to reply in a thread. This keeps the conversation history clean and easy to reference later.

If you manage multiple workspaces, use the workspace switcher in the top left corner. You can also use Command + Shift + bracket keys to cycle through your workspaces quickly. For recruiters working across different time zones, use the scheduling feature. Click the arrow next to the send button to schedule a message for when your hiring manager is actually online.

Keep your sidebar organized by starring important channels. Right click on a channel name and select Star this channel. These will move to the top of your sidebar under a dedicated section. This simple step ensures that your most active hiring projects are always just one click away.

Slack can become heavy on memory if you have many channels open. If you notice the app lagging, check your activity monitor. Sometimes clearing the cache is enough to restore performance. If you are on an older Mac, consider disabling animations in the accessibility settings of the Slack preferences menu.

faq.question: How do I find a message I read earlier?
faq.answer: Use the search bar at the top of the app. Type in:channelname or from:username to narrow down your results.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to reply to messages?
faq.answer: Lazur helps you draft and dictate text. You can use your voice to type out your message and then press Enter to send it.

faq.question: How do I stop Slack from distracting me?
faq.answer: Use the /dnd command to pause notifications for a specific time period. You can also set a notification schedule in your preferences.
